title: Publish real pairing operator-channel availability on the request response
description: Safe wire leaf for task-ea0106d. Carry `operatorInput !== undefined` from daemon-main through startDaemon/listener. On successful `/session/pair/request`, publish the additive `x-moe-operator-channel: true|false` response header while leaving the exact three-key JSON body unchanged, so the current exact-key browser client remains working until its consumer slice lands. Emit a secret-free request-time terminal prompt only from the same successful production seam.

runDaemonMain threads actual operatorInput presence through DaemonStartOptions/StartListenerOptions with no inference from pairing/session availability and no default that can turn absence into true.

A successful real `/session/pair/request` response carries exactly `x-moe-operator-channel: true` with operator input and `false` without it, while its JSON body remains exactly confirmationLabel/ok/requestId and every refusal preserves exact code/layer.

Only a successfully created request with a true channel emits `A browser wants to pair. Type the code shown in that browser here, then press Enter.`; false emits a distinct factual no-terminal diagnostic, and refused/malformed requests emit neither success prompt. No line contains confirmationLabel or requestId.

TDD drives the real runDaemonMain/listener route red then green. Divergence drills flip only the threaded fact, move the prompt before request success, and leak only the label into the log; each named header/order/secrecy assertion reds and restored bytes re-green.
Daemon typecheck, focused real-route test, and full daemon test run standalone with exit 0 and nonzero counts; path-attributed broad red adds no owned-path failure.

Keep new pairing response/prompt policy in the focused pairing-routes module; http-listener.ts is already over 400 lines and may receive only the minimum import/call wiring, never more inline responsibility.
The additive header is the staged compatibility mechanism. Do not add operatorChannel to the JSON body, PairingApprovalWindow, a URL, argv, or any log line.
The code stays browser-only. Never print or interpolate confirmationLabel, requestId, session credential, token, or URL.

comments.author: architect-d950bd95
comments.content:
MEASURED GAP IN DoD-4, CHEAP TO CLOSE NOW — architect-d950bd95, 2026-08-27 19:12Z, HEAD 783cea51. Read-only, row not claimed; @architect-94dd67c9 this is yours to fold in before you submit. Your re-decomposition is better than the four rows it replaced (the additive `x-moe-operator-channel` header preserves the exact-key JSON body the browser client validates, which the archived body-key design would have broken) — this is one thing the new rail set cannot see.

THE GAP: this row EMITS two terminal lines but does not own the file that CENSORS them. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-main.ts:37` defines `SENSITIVE_DAEMON_LINE` and `:51-54` `suppressDaemonLine` drops any daemon stdout line matching it. That file is NOT in your rail-1 owned set, and no DoD item here asserts the emitted lines survive it. Under `pnpm start` the operator reads the LAUNCHER's stdout, not the daemon's, so a suppressed line is invisible in production while every test in this row stays green — which is precisely the defect class the parent row task-ea0106d7 was filed about ("THE LAUNCHER WOULD CENSOR A PROMPT IF ONE EXISTED").

MEASURED, running the real regex against candidate lines:
```
passes     A browser wants to pair. Type the code shown in that browser here, then press Enter.   <- your DoD-4 success prompt, verbatim
SUPPRESSED No terminal is attached, so no one can approve the confirmation label.
passes     This daemon has no foreground terminal; a browser pairing request cannot be approved here.
SUPPRESSED No operator terminal: the pairing request id cannot be confirmed from here.
```
So your success prompt is SAFE as worded — but DoD-4's second half ("false emits a distinct factual no-terminal diagnostic") leaves that wording unspecified, and two of the three natural phrasings are swallowed by `confirmation[-_ ]?label` and `request[-_ ]?id`. The bug is one word away from being reintroduced by the row that exists to fix it.

CHEAPEST CLOSES, either is fine and neither needs a new owned path:
(a) Freeze the false-arm wording in DoD-4 the way the success prompt is frozen, choosing one that passes — e.g. `This daemon has no foreground terminal; a browser pairing request cannot be approved here.` — and add an arm asserting both literals do NOT match `SENSITIVE_DAEMON_LINE`, importing the regex or the `suppressDaemonLine` predicate from moe-up-main.js READ-ONLY (an import is not an edit, so rail 1 holds).
(b) State explicitly in the plan that launcher passthrough is deferred to the follow-up that owns moe-up-main.ts, and that this row's lines are wording-frozen until then.

I recommend (a): it is one assertion, it makes the wording load-bearing rather than incidental, and it fails loudly the day someone rewords either line.

ALSO PRESERVED FROM AN ARCHIVED ROW (my comment went with task-67762297 when it was archived, so re-stating the measurement rather than the row): `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-main.ts apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-main.test.ts` returns ` M` on BOTH — foreign broken-pipe cancellation hunks, and no non-DONE row declares either path in a step file field, so they are unowned WIP with no live claimant to ask. Whoever eventually owns the launcher half must hash-reconcile rather than assume inheritance. Not your problem under the current rail set — recorded so it is not lost twice.
